human_tolerance.notes: Secretive; avoids open areas and human activity (en.wikipedia). Sings more loudly in urban or near-urban areas where it occurs (en.wikipedia), so the affinity is a judgement that the bird is not a garden species.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Migrates south from early September; wintering quarters in sub-Saharan Africa; returns north from mid-March to early April (fr.wikipedia, Migration). Month-day boundaries are rounded from that text.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeding season runs from late April to mid-July in Europe (fr.wikipedia, Reproduction).

inat.skipped_reason: permissive GBIF tier A is usable; non-commercial iNaturalist tier C excluded

vocalizations.description: Loud, powerful and highly varied song of whistles, trills and gurgles, with a loud whistling crescendo; phrases of two to four seconds separated by pauses of similar length.
A frog-like alarm call given when the bird is disturbed.

taxonomy.note: GBIF usage key 7660710 is ACCEPTED at SPECIES rank (checked 2026-10-31); ITIS TSN 560897 is a valid species record with the same name. Authority from GBIF canonical name.

external.note: GBIF key checked at api.gbif.org; iNaturalist taxon 13079 (Luscinia megarhynchos, species rank, active) checked at api.inaturalist.org. ITIS TSN, NCBI taxon 383689 (Wikidata P685), eBird comnig1 (Wikidata P3444) and iNaturalist (Wikidata P3151) agree with the records.

conservation.note: Wikidata IUCN conservation status claim (P141) resolves to 'least concern'. IUCN pages are not openly licensed, so the status was not copied from the IUCN site.

range.note: Derived from the range descriptions: the English article gives western Europe, North Africa and Asia Minor; the French article gives a northern limit at southern England and northern Germany, eastward to central Poland and southern Ukraine, and North Africa from Morocco to Tunisia. The list is not exhaustive and was not checked country by country. Activity was fetched for FR only.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Flight is sourced (migratory bird). The sources describe foraging on the ground among leaves but give no gait. Hop is a judgement shared with other ground-feeding passerines; walking was not added because no source gives it.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Bird; endothermy is standard for Aves and is not stated explicitly in the sources.

traits.nest_type.note: 'It nests on or near the ground in dense vegetation' (en). 'Son nid est peu ordonné et bas (rarement au-dessus de 50 cm), voire à même le sol' (fr).

traits.perching.note: Males sing 'from concealed perches' in dense shrubs (en).

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 19.6 g, source Dunning08 (SpecID 9213). The French article gives 16 to 39 g without a source; that range was not used.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Animal Diversity Web, Lifespan/Longevity: typical lifespan, status wild, 1 to 5 years. The field requires one number, so 3 years is the arithmetic midpoint of that reported range, not a separately observed average. The separate oldest recorded age (8 years 4 months) is not used. The adult apparent-survival conversion from Scholer et al. (2020) was removed because it does not estimate the schema field directly. Checked alternative: BTO BirdFacts reports 2 years for a UK bird reaching breeding age (https://www.bto.org/learn/about-birds/birdfacts/nightingale); the source page does not provide an allow-listed licence, so it is not used. ADW is used only for this required field as the last-resort CC BY-NC-SA source; permissive sources checked (BTO BirdFacts and the existing CC BY-SA Wikipedia articles) did not support this exact typical-wild lifespan value.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 70, Diet-Fruit 20, Diet-Seed 10 (BirdFuncDat.txt, SpecID 9213). The French article says the bird eats mainly invertebrates year-round, plus fruit and seeds in late summer and autumn. The source gives no vertebrate, fish or carrion share, so none is included.

traits.social.note: Territorial; only unpaired males sing regularly at night, and pairs form in the breeding season. Group size [1,2] is a judgement from that text.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal = 0, so the pattern is Diurnal. The article says males sing frequently at night as well as by day. Night song is therefore handled in the species-local behaviour program, not in this field.

traits.defense.note: 'Often remain motionless when they sense a potential threat' (en) maps to Freeze.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 'elusive and secretive birds' (en). Not a measured value.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-ground 70, ForStrat-understory 30 (understory mapped to arboreal, as in the robin record).

habitat.shelter_tag.note: 'Spending much of their time hidden in dense shrubs, thickets, and undergrowth' (en).

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrate weight from EltonTraits Diet-Inv. Fruit and seed months from the French article (late summer and autumn, mapped to Aug–Nov). Nest site from the English article (ground in dense vegetation). Shelter weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Avoids open areas and human activity (en). The urban singing note is recorded in the notes field; no numeric tolerance is claimed.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'A migratory insectivorous species' (en); 'un grand migrateur nocturne' (fr).

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding late April to mid-July and absence from early September to late March, both for France only. The French article gives the timing for Europe generally, so France is the only region this record supports. Other regions need their own phases.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Only the adult stage is declared; juvenile timing is not needed for the current behaviour.

vocalizations.song.note: Loud and varied song, singing day and night (en, fr). Season months 4 to 7 follow the breeding window; the French article says it sings mainly at night to attract a mate. Cooldown 8 s is the shared program default, not a sourced value.

vocalizations.alarm.note: 'It has a frog-like alarm call' (en). Cooldown 5 s and loudness are judgement.

look.note: Colours and proportions are authored from 'plain brown above except for the reddish tail; buff to white below'. Tail length is authored.

behavior.note: Species-local bt-nightingale-v1: derived from bt-perching-songbird-v1 with night song in breeding months, nest site on the ground and month sets from the sources. Shared program rests at night and sings only in the -6 to 12 degree sun window, which the sources contradict. See behavior.json.
